Klassische Suche und die KI-Funktionen d: Classic search and the AI features of Google Search rest, at Google, on the same foundation: technically reachable, indexable content in textual form that matches what is visible on the page. And the same foundation has the same limits — robots.txt governs the request, not the appearance, and no requirement met is a promise.
Google nennt für die eigene Suche techni: For its own search, Google names technical minimum requirements for a page to be eligible for indexing at all. There are three: Googlebot is not blocked, the page responds with the status code HTTP 200, and the page has indexable content. The caveat follows immediately — that a page meets these requirements does not mean it will be indexed; indexing is not guaranteed.
Für die KI-Funktionen der eigenen Suche: For the AI features of its own search, Google describes the same foundation. For a page to be able to appear as a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode, it must be indexed, eligible to be shown with a snippet, and fulfil the technical requirements of Search; there are no additional technical requirements. Here too the source places the caveat right behind it: indexing and serving are not guaranteed.
Ein Sondermarkup verlangt Google für die: Nor does Google require any special markup for these features. By its own account, no new machine readable files, no AI text files and no special schema.org markup are needed to appear in them; files such as llms.txt or Markdown versions of a page are not used by Google Search itself — not for its generative features either. That is a statement about Google Search and about nothing else.
Daraus wird leicht eine gemeinsame Anbie: It is easy to turn this into a shared provider line that does not exist on the pages examined. Google says, for its own generative search, that no special markup is needed. Microsoft gives its own content recommendations in the product documentation of Bing Webmaster Tools, without promising an outcome. Anyone who pulls both into a single rule is stacking two self-descriptions of two different systems on top of each other.
Was danach übrig bleibt, ist unspektakul: What remains after that is unspectacular and the same for all three questions. Pixelkiez examines it as four building blocks — the grouping is our own, the individual requirements behind it come from the sources named below.

Zugänge, Statuscode, robots.txt. Genau d: Access, status code, robots.txt. That is precisely what Google lists as minimum requirements: an unblocked Googlebot, a page that responds with HTTP 200, and indexable content.
Stehen Name, Leistung, Ort und Kontaktwe: Are name, service, location and contact route on the page as text?
Google führt als Praxis auf, wichtige In: Google lists as a practice making sure that important content is available in textual form. That clear or consistent company details secure rankings, mentions or inclusion in a knowledge graph is stated on none of the pages examined here — this building block concerns whether a detail can be found, not what it achieves.
Steht die Antwort auf die Frage, um die: Is the answer to the question at hand written out on the page?
Was ein System übernehmen soll, muss auf: What a system is meant to take over has to be on the page in the first place. How strongly a written-out detail works compared with scattered hints is stated by none of the provider pages examined — this building block describes what is present, not what it brings about.
Passt die Auszeichnung zu dem, was ein M: Does the markup match what a human reads on the page?
Google führt es ausdrücklich als Praxis: Google explicitly lists as a practice making sure your structured data matches the visible text on the page. No special markup needed therefore does not mean that markup is irrelevant — it means that Google requires no additional markup for these features.
Ein Missverständnis gehört an dieser Ste: One misunderstanding belongs cleared up at this point.
Die robots.txt ist eine Abrufsteuerung,: The robots.txt file is a crawl control, not a lock and not a delete button.
Google beschreibt sie als Datei, die Suc: Google describes it as a file that tells search engine crawlers which URLs they may access on the site, and states in the same paragraph: it is not a mechanism for keeping a web page out of Google. Anyone who wants that should block indexing with noindex or password-protect the page.
Die Grenzen benennt dieselbe Seite selbs: The same page names the limits itself. A page disallowed in robots.txt can still be indexed if other sites link to it — Google phrases this as a possibility, not as the rule. Its URL may then appear in the search results, though without a description. And the instructions in the file cannot enforce crawler behaviour: whether they are obeyed is up to the crawler in question, and the rules may not be supported by all search engines. As the route intended for properly preventing a URL from appearing in Google Search results, Google names password protection on the server, the noindex meta tag or the corresponding response header, or removing the page entirely.
Der Robots-Standard selbst sagt dasselbe: The robots standard itself says the same in one sentence: the rules in a robots.txt file are not a form of access authorisation. Whether the file steers AI systems, incidentally, is not stated on the Google introduction page examined — it speaks of search engine crawlers and of Googlebot.
Bei OpenAI kommt zur Freigabe eine zweit: With OpenAI a second condition is added to permission. So that a website appears in search results, OpenAI recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot in the site's robots.txt file and allowing requests from its published IP ranges. On the Anthropic help page examined there is no comparable condition. About further providers these two pages say nothing.
Über allem steht ein Satz, den Google se: Above all of this stands a sentence Google itself wrote into the Search Essentials: even if a page meets all of the requirements and best practices there, that does not mean Google will crawl, index or serve its content.
Wer Präsenz in KI-Antworten messen will,: Anyone who wants to measure presence in AI answers will find one counting mechanism at Google and one at Microsoft — and the two count different things. What comes out of it also depends on when, where and in which system the measurement was taken.
Vorweg eine Einordnung in eigener Sache:: A note on our own account first: the heading of this section is ours. No provider document sets measurement against optimisation — Google's guide is itself an optimisation guide, and Microsoft's help article has a section of its own with content recommendations. What the providers do very much do for their own figures is something else: they promise no outcome.

Für die Frage, wie Inhalte in den genera: For the question of how content performs in the generative AI features, Google points to a report of its own in Search Console. What is counted there are impressions: how many times links to your site were shown to a user in a generative AI feature on Google Search. This can be grouped by pages, countries, dates and devices; a dimension for individual search queries is not listed in the help article.
Bing Webmaster Tools: Zitationen als Zäh: Bing Webmaster Tools: citations as the counted quantity
Im AI-Performance-Bericht der Bing Webma: The AI Performance report in Bing Webmaster Tools carries the metric Total Citations. Below it, the help article describes it as the total number of times content from your own site was visibly referenced or shown as a source in AI-generated answers during the selected date range. Next to it stands Citation Share: according to Microsoft's announcement, the percentage of citations attributed to your own site out of all citations shown across all sites for that same grounding query. Microsoft distinguishes the two explicitly — one says how often something was cited, the other what share of the citation space a site receives for a specific grounding query.
Bei OpenAI ist das Messbare ein Verweisp: With OpenAI the measurable thing is a referral parameter: to referral URLs from ChatGPT search, ChatGPT appends utm_source=chatgpt.com, which allows clear analysis of inbound traffic. The precondition, according to the same source, is that OAI-SearchBot may access the content. What is measured with it are clicks, not mentions.
Seit Juni 2026 hat Microsoft diesen Beri: Since June 2026 Microsoft has extended this report by four capabilities: Intents, Topics, Citation Share and Compare. The announcement post carries them as a preview — “in preview” — and states in the availability section that they are beginning to roll out globally. Whether every account sees them today is stated by none of the pages examined. Intents classifies the grounding queries in the AI Performance report into broader categories such as Informational, Commercial, Navigational, Learn and Solve, Research, Creation, Local and more; the post itself treats this classification as provisional.
Der bemerkenswerteste Satz zu diesen Zah: The most remarkable sentence about these figures comes from Microsoft itself. Citation Share is, by its own account, designed as an observational metric — not a ranking system and not a competitive scoreboard; the metric shows neither competitor domains nor traffic share nor quality scores. That is a statement about the intent behind the metric, not a finding verified from outside.
Google warnt in derselben Sache vor Werk: On the same matter Google warns about tools that promise ranking success or claim to use internal Google metrics: no third-party tool has access to Google's internal ranking or AI systems. That is not a blanket rejection — in the same paragraph Google writes that you should feel free to use such tools if they help your workflow, but measure their advice against the official documentation.
Was eine Messung ergibt, hängt von den U: What a measurement yields depends on the circumstances — and that is by the providers' own account. Google names time, location, language and personalisation as reasons why search results may differ between people, and states on the same page that you may also get the same or similar results as someone else. For ChatGPT, OpenAI describes that a VPN or the network location may affect the approximate location inferred from the IP address, and that saved location information may also influence search results. And for search results it can, according to OpenAI, take around 24 hours for a change to robots.txt to be reflected in their systems.
Daraus folgt eine Methode, und zwar unse: A method follows from this — ours, not a provider's.
Pixelkiez beobachtet AI Visibility an ei: Pixelkiez observes AI Visibility against a set of questions fixed in advance, in a named system, at a recorded point in time and in a recorded language and country version. None of the provider pages examined names this evaluation, recommends it or requires it. It makes an observation traceable — a promise about future answers does not follow from it.
Google sagt über die eigene Suche, dass: Google says about its own search that the SEO fundamentals stay relevant because the generative features are rooted in the core systems of Search. Microsoft says about its own index that grounding does not replace search but builds on the same infrastructure. OpenAI says about its own search that it sometimes partners with other search providers. Three providers, three self-descriptions of three of their own systems — this section claims no more than that.
Googles Leitfaden stellt die Frage, ob S: Google's guide asks whether SEO is still relevant for generative AI search and answers yes: the established SEO best practices remain relevant because the generative AI features of Google Search are rooted in its core Search ranking and quality systems. Elsewhere the same page describes these systems more precisely — the core ranking systems focus on high-quality content, other systems block spam, and the generative AI features depend on both groups of systems. The bullet point this stands under warns against seeking inauthentic mentions; it notes in the same breath that the generative features can show what is being said about products and services across the web.
Wie oft die KI-Antwortfläche überhaupt e: How often the AI answer surface appears at all is described by Google with restraint: AI Overviews are only shown when Google's systems determine that they are additive to classic Search, and accordingly often do not trigger. That is not a criterion site owners can check from outside — it is a decision made by the systems. For control, Google points to the robots.txt directives for Googlebot, which manage how pages are crawled for Search; to limit what is shown, the same section names nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet and noindex, and for training and grounding in some of Google's other systems it points to Google-Extended.
Microsoft argumentiert in einem Beitrag: Microsoft argues in a post on its own Bing blog about the role of the index. The classic model of crawling, quality evaluation and ranking has worked extraordinarily well — and still does. In a section of its own about two systems with two responsibilities it says that traditional search and grounding systems share the same foundation of crawling, understanding and ranking the web, but are optimised for fundamentally different outcomes. A further section explicitly clears up a common misconception: grounding does not replace search. It builds on the same foundational infrastructure — the same crawlers, the same quality signals, the same deep understanding of the web — and adds a new optimisation layer on top. Summed up there in two sentences: the infrastructure is shared. The purpose is different.
Wichtig für die Einordnung: Dieser Beitr: Important for placing this: the post is a position piece by four Microsoft authors on the company blog. It describes and justifies an index strategy; it is not product documentation and not a specification for site owners.
OpenAI sagt über die eigene Suche einen: About its own search OpenAI says a third, quite different sentence: ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers and then typically rewrites the question into one or more targeted queries sent to those providers. Which providers those are is not named in the body text of this page — and sometimes means sometimes.
Ein Nebenbefund betrifft die Zählung: We: One side finding concerns counting: sites appearing in Google's AI features are, according to Google, included in the overall search traffic in Search Console just like the rest of the search results page. That describes how Search Console counts — not how the systems relate to one another.
Was daraus folgt, ist eine Einordnung un: What follows from this is an interpretation, not a market finding.
Pixelkiez liest die drei Selbstaussagen: Pixelkiez reads the three self-descriptions as coexistence: classic findability and presence in answer systems exist side by side, and neither of the two is settled by the other. No provider document examined formulates this thesis — each speaks only about its own systems. Examined here are Google, Microsoft and OpenAI; about Anthropic, Perplexity or other providers this section says nothing, not even a denial. And there is deliberately no figure in this section: on market share, usage share or lost clicks, no value is available from the documents named below.
Was sich beobachten lässt — und was nich: What can be observed — and what cannot.
Beobachtbar ist der prüfbare Zustand ein: Observable are the checkable state of a page, the measured referral traffic and whatever a provider counts itself. Not verifiable is whether a system names a particular page — and on the pages examined here, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI each rule out such a promise themselves.
Was sich messen und wiederholen lässt: What can be measured and repeated
Der Zustand einer Seite: Statuscodes, We: The state of a page: status codes, redirects, robots.txt, and whether the load-bearing details are in the delivered document. Alongside that, the referral traffic ChatGPT marks with its parameter — clicks, not mentions. And whatever a provider counts itself: impressions in Search Console, citations in the AI Performance report of Bing Webmaster Tools.
Was sich mit Gründen ableiten lässt: What can be derived with reasons
Microsoft schreibt, die gezeigten Werte: Microsoft writes that the values shown represent a sample of overall citation activity and may be refined as additional data is processed. It follows that a zero in the report is not evidence of a zero in reality. How large the gap is does not follow from it: Microsoft names neither share nor coverage nor margin of error — an estimate would be invented at this point.
Ob ein KI-System eine bestimmte Seite in: Whether an AI system names a particular page in a particular answer cannot be established beforehand and afterwards only for the answers actually observed. Equally open: what happens to user-triggered requests once they have been made. On the pages examined from OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity this is not documented.
Die Anbieter sind an dieser Stelle deutl: On this point the providers are clearer than the market that talks about them. Google states that it does not guarantee it will crawl, index or serve a page — not even if the page follows the Google Search Essentials. For the AI features the same sentence appears again: even if a page meets all requirements and best practices and complies with the policies, that does not mean Google will crawl, index or serve its content; indexing and serving are not guaranteed. The same holds for structured data — correct markup does not force a display. And on ranking promises Google becomes fundamental: no one can guarantee a first place in Google; the same page explicitly warns about providers who guarantee rankings, allege a special relationship with Google or advertise priority submission.
Microsoft zieht die Grenzen für den eige: Microsoft draws the limits for its own report just as clearly. The AI Performance report does not measure rankings, authority, performance or importance; it simply shows which content was cited. Improving content quality, structure and freshness can help strengthen content, but does not guarantee a specific citation outcome. And the causal inference is explicitly ruled out: Citation Share can help you observe whether your own share changes over time after content updates, but it does not establish a causal link.
OpenAI beschreibt für ChatGPT, wonach di: For ChatGPT, OpenAI describes what search results are ordered by, and states in the same section: placement is not guaranteed. The same page names two conditions for a website to be eligible for inclusion at all — OAI-Searchbot may crawl the site, and the host or content delivery network allows traffic from the published searchbot IP addresses. In the other direction: if OpenAI obtains the address of a disallowed page from another source and has signals that the page is relevant to the user's query, just the link with the page title may surface in ChatGPT Atlas. The source names the remedy right along with it — the noindex meta tag.
Bei nutzerausgelösten Abrufen gehen die: On user-triggered requests the three documents examined diverge. Perplexity writes about its own user-triggered fetcher that it generally ignores robots.txt because a user requested the fetch. OpenAI writes for the corresponding requests that robots.txt rules may not apply because the action is initiated by a user. Anthropic commits its bots across the board to the industry standard directives in robots.txt, without making a separate promise for the user-triggered fetcher. That holds for exactly these three pages.
Der Robots-Standard sagt dazu das Nötige: The robots standard says what is needed here: it is not a substitute for valid content security measures, and listing paths makes them publicly discoverable. And Google names one gap in the figures itself — data from experiments in Search Labs is not included in Search Console, because those experiments are still in active development.
Aus einem Garantieausschluss folgt nicht: Nothing follows in the opposite direction from an exclusion of guarantees.
Dass niemand eine Nennung zusagt, heißt: That no one promises a mention does not mean a mention is unlikely; it means the question can only be answered by observation. Anyone who assures you of a mention in AI answers or a place in search is promising something the providers of these systems explicitly do not promise for themselves.
Die Aussagen oben stützen sich auf die f: The statements above rest on the following primary sources. Provider statements describe what a provider says about its own system — which makes them the best available source and at the same time changeable at any time.

Wie KI Ihre Website wirklich liest: How AI really reads your website
Crawler, KI-Suchsysteme und Browser-Agen: Crawlers, AI search systems and browser agents call up the same address — and do not necessarily get the same thing to look at. This article sorts out what arrives on the first request, why that differs between systems, and what follows from it for a company website.
Besuchertypen nach ihrem Zweck untersche: Telling visitor types apart by purpose
Direkten Abruf und Browser-Rendering tre: Separating a direct request from browser rendering
Es gibt nicht die eine maschinelle Sicht: There is no single machine view of your website.
Wenn ein Mensch Ihre Website öffnet, pas: When a person opens your website, a fair amount happens in the background: the browser loads the document, runs scripts, fetches images and fonts, and assembles the page that finally appears on screen. That result is so self-evident that it is easily mistaken for the website itself.
Maschinelle Besucher gehen diesen Weg ni: Machine visitors do not necessarily follow that path. Some fetch the document and read the delivered text. Others run the page in a real browser and see the finished interface. Others again come mainly to get something done on the page rather than to read it.
Deshalb lässt sich die Frage „Was sieht: That is why the question “What does AI see on my website?” cannot be answered in that form. It becomes answerable only with three additions: which system, for which purpose, by which route. Those three questions run through this whole article.
Nicht jeder maschinelle Besucher kommt a: Not every machine visitor comes for the same reason.
Automatisierte Zugriffe lassen sich nach: Automated requests can be sorted by purpose. The grouping below is an orientation aid, not an official taxonomy — but it explains why the same website is treated differently by different systems.
Ein System erfasst Inhalte, um sie späte: A system records content so that it can later show and link it in search results or answers. OpenAI names OAI-SearchBot for this: anyone who wants content to appear in summaries and snippets in ChatGPT must not block that access. Anthropic describes Claude-SearchBot as a bot meant to improve the quality of search results. Perplexity describes PerplexityBot as designed to surface and link websites in search results.
Modellentwicklung — und deren Steuerung: Model development — and how to control it
Beim zweiten Zweck geht es um Inhalte, d: The second purpose concerns content that may feed into the development of models, and above all how a site owner controls that. OpenAI points to GPTBot for this: anyone who wants to exclude pages from potential training should disallow that user agent. Anthropic writes about ClaudeBot that it collects content which could potentially contribute to their training. Perplexity draws an explicit line here: PerplexityBot is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models.
Abruf im Auftrag eines Nutzers: A request on behalf of a user
Beim dritten Fall steht der unmittelbare: The third case centres on the immediate user request: a person asks a question, and the provider can fetch web content specifically for it. Anthropic describes Claude-User that way — when people ask Claude something, Claude may access websites through that agent. Perplexity describes Perplexity-User accordingly and states explicitly that this fetcher generally ignores robots.txt, because a user triggered the request. Nothing general follows from this about how providers subsequently store or further process such fetches.
Für viele automatisierte Crawler ist ein: For many automated crawlers, a single file in the root directory is the central means of control: robots.txt. Anthropic writes that its own bots honour the industry-standard directives in it. How user-triggered requests behave, by contrast, depends on the provider and on the type of access: Perplexity states explicitly for Perplexity-User that this fetcher generally ignores robots.txt for user-requested fetches. Robots.txt is therefore a control and not a lock.
Ein häufiges Missverständnis gehört glei: A common misunderstanding belongs right here:
Google-Extended is not a bot of its own.
Googles Crawler-Dokumentation hält fest,: Google’s crawler documentation states that Google-Extended has no separate user agent string in HTTP requests; crawling is done with the existing Google user agents, and the entry in robots.txt works purely as a control. It governs whether content Google has crawled may be used for training future Gemini models and for grounding in certain Google products. On inclusion in Google Search and on ranking there it has, according to the same documentation, no influence.
Dieselbe URL kann je nach System und Abr: Depending on the system and the retrieval path, the same URL can arrive as a rendered interface, as text or as structured fields. The representation alone does not reveal which path a specific system uses on each retrieval.
Was bekommt ein System beim ersten Abruf: What does a system get on the first request?
Am einfachsten wird das an einem Beispie: This is easiest to show with an example. Take a fictional business: Elektro Koenig Berlin, focus on wallbox installation, location Berlin, desired action “request an appointment”. Four details a person finds in seconds. Whether a machine finds them depends on the route it takes.
Die Fakten stehen im ausgelieferten Doku: The facts are in the delivered document
Der Server liefert die Angaben bereits m: The server delivers the details already. A system that only reads the delivered document and runs no browser has the name, the service, the location and the desired action together straight away.
Der Inhalt entsteht erst im Browser: The content only comes into being in the browser
Google nennt diesen Aufbau das App-Shell: Google calls this structure the app shell model: the first HTML does not contain the actual content; it only comes into being once a browser runs the scripts. Anyone reading without a browser finds an empty frame at this point. Anyone reading with a browser sees the same page as a person.
Ein System, das die Seite tatsächlich in: A system that actually runs the page in a browser gets the finished interface: heading, text, buttons. It does not only read — it also sees what can be operated.
Ein verbreiteter Kurzschluss lautet: Was: A common short circuit runs: whatever is not there as running text in the source does not exist for machines. It is not that simple. The delivered document holds more than the visible text — structured data, embedded data blocks and server-prepared content are in there too, and they are readable. The dividing line does not run between visible and invisible, but between what the server delivers and what only the browser creates.
Und eine Einschränkung gehört dazu: Das: And a limitation belongs with it: the example sorts routes. It does not describe the architecture of any particular provider — which route a specific system takes on a specific request is not settled by it.
Rendering is not the same everywhere.
Ob ein System JavaScript ausführt, ist k: Whether a system runs JavaScript is not a property of “AI”, but a property of that particular system. For some of these systems there is a solid measurement — with a clear date and clear limits.
Vercel and MERJ published an analysis of actual requests on 17 December 2024. For the specialised AI crawlers examined there — named are OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User and GPTBot from OpenAI, ClaudeBot from Anthropic, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bytespider and PerplexityBot — the result was: they ran no JavaScript. In part they even downloaded JavaScript files without executing them.
Zwei Gegenbeispiele in derselben Studie: Two counter-examples in the same study
Dieselbe Auswertung nennt zwei Systeme,: The same analysis names two systems that do render: Gemini used Google’s infrastructure and could therefore render fully, and AppleBot renders, according to the same source, through a browser-based crawler. “No JavaScript” is thus not even within this study a property of all AI-related requests. On top of that comes the tense: the study explicitly described the state at that time. It is a dated measurement, not a promise about every request today.
Was das für eine Website bedeutet: What that means for a website
Eine Frage statt einer Regel: A question instead of a rule
Daraus folgt kein pauschales „alles serv: No blanket “render everything on the server” follows from this. What follows is a question every business can answer for itself: which details that matter commercially only come into being in the browser? For the service, the location, the price range and the contact route, a dependency on the browser is an avoidable risk. For an image slider or a chat window it is less critical, as long as no commercially load-bearing detail and no necessary action is available exclusively through that component.
Für die klassische Google-Suche ist der: For classic Google Search the case is documented and different: Google Search runs JavaScript, with a continuously updated version of Chromium. The documentation describes three phases for this — crawling, rendering, indexing — and states at the same time that these phases do not run cleanly one after another and are not observable from outside.
Beides gleichzeitig ist damit möglich: G: Both at once is therefore possible: Google can render client-side generated content and process it for indexing, while a non-rendering request receives only the document as initially delivered. Anyone who looks only at Google visibility does not see that difference.
Readable does not yet mean visible.
Technische Erreichbarkeit ist die erste: Technical reachability is the first stage, not the last. In its analysis Pixelkiez keeps four questions apart, because they are answered in different ways — and because an early stage never proves a later one.
Kann ein System die Seite überhaupt abru: Can a system fetch the page at all?
Zugänge, Weiterleitungen, Statuscodes, r: Access, redirects, status codes, robots.txt. Without an open door nothing further happens.
Lassen sich die Fakten zuverlässig herau: Can the facts be extracted reliably?
Leistung, Ort, Zuständigkeit, Kontaktweg: Service, location, responsibility, contact route — as text a system can assign unambiguously, not merely as an impression.
Beantwortet die Seite eine konkrete Frag: Does the page answer a concrete question unambiguously?
Aus lesbaren Angaben wird nicht automati: Readable details do not automatically become an answer that can be adopted. For that, the question has to be genuinely answered on the page.
Taucht die Domain in KI-Antworten tatsäc: Does the domain actually appear in AI answers?
Das zeigt sich nur in einem definierten,: That shows only in a defined, repeatable test — observed, not inferred.
Erreichbar ist eine Voraussetzung — kein: Being reachable is a precondition — not proof of visibility.
Stufe 1 belegt Stufe 4 nicht. Dass ein C: Stage 1 does not prove stage 4. That a crawler is allowed to fetch a page says nothing about whether it ever appears in an answer.
Die Anbieter selbst formulieren das übri: The providers themselves put this more cautiously than the industry often repeats it. OpenAI describes allowing OAI-SearchBot as the precondition for a website to be eligible for inclusion at all, and states in the same section: placement is not guaranteed.
An agent does not come only to read.
Ein Browser-Agent unterscheidet sich gru: A browser agent differs fundamentally from a simple request. It is given an interface and a task — and for that it needs not only text, but controls that can be named.
Ein Abruf liefert ein Dokument. Ein Agen: A request delivers a document. An agent stands in front of an interface and is meant to get something done on it. Whether it succeeds depends on whether the page declares its controls as what they are: a button as a button, a form field with a label, a menu with a recognisable state.
OpenAI nennt dafür ein konkretes Beispie: OpenAI names a concrete example for this: ChatGPT Atlas uses ARIA tags — the same roles and labels that screen readers evaluate — to interpret page structure and interactive elements. The recommendation is to follow WAI-ARIA best practices and give interactive elements such as buttons, menus and forms descriptive roles, labels and states.
Dieser Punkt wird leicht falsch verstand: This point is easily misread, so plainly:
Accessibility is not an AI trick.
Sie ist zuerst dafür da, dass Menschen e: It exists first of all so that people can use a website — with a screen reader, with the keyboard, with limited sight. That semantic roles, labels and states can additionally help browser agents is something OpenAI currently documents explicitly for agent operation in ChatGPT Atlas — the recommendation just mentioned. No general assurance for agents at large comes with it.
Geschäftlich interessant wird das dort,: It becomes commercially interesting where an action stands at the end: finding a way to make contact, choosing a service, sending an enquiry, starting a booking. What a particular agent actually carries through of that today is explicitly not settled here — the range is wide and keeps changing. The durable statement is more modest: a page whose controls are unnamed makes it harder than necessary for an agent that goes by that markup — and for some of your human visitors as well.
What companies should watch out for today.
Fünf robuste Grundsätze für Websites, di: Five robust principles for websites that are meant to stay understandable and usable across different access paths.
Tragende Angaben gehören ins ausgeliefer: Load-bearing details belong in the delivered document.
Geschäftlich tragende Informationen soll: Load-bearing business information should not depend unnecessarily on one particular rendering path. Name, service, location, price range and contact route are typical examples. Which information is load-bearing depends on the individual website.
Entscheiden Sie Zugänge bewusst statt ve: Decide on access deliberately rather than by accident.
In der robots.txt lassen sich Suche und: In robots.txt, search and model development can be governed separately; for user-triggered requests the effect depends on the provider and on the type of access. Blanket blocking can also shut out systems through which content is meant to be findable.
Beantworten Sie Fragen dort, wo sie gest: Answer questions where they are asked.
Zentrale Angaben, die ausschließlich in: Central details that exist exclusively in PDFs or images are not equally reliably accessible across every request and answer path; what exists only on a phone call is not on the page at all. Prices, catchment areas, deadlines and responsibilities should therefore additionally be present as plain HTML text on the page.
Beschriftete Schaltflächen und Formularf: Labelled buttons and form fields, correct roles, a structure that can be followed. This helps people first — and can make the page easier to operate for agents that go by that markup.
Behandeln Sie Sichtbarkeit als Messgröße: Treat visibility as something measured, not as something promised.
Ob eine Domain in KI-Antworten auftaucht: Whether a domain appears in AI answers can be checked — with defined, repeatable tests. Anyone claiming it without such tests is merely claiming it.
